name: Relume
subcategory: AI wireframing and component library for Webflow
tagline: AI generates a sitemap and wireframes, then hands you real responsive sections you can paste straight into Webflow, Figma, or React.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The AI part of Relume is the easy part: prompting a model for a sitemap and a per-page list of sections is a couple of hours of work. The hard part is the thing behind it, hundreds of hand-built, genuinely responsive sections that look designed rather than generated, plus the clipboard format that drops them into Webflow without breaking. An agent can absolutely give you a local generator that outputs Tailwind and React sections from a library you seed yourself, and if you write React that is a real replacement. If your actual workflow ends in Webflow or a Figma handoff, you are rebuilding an export pipeline, not a website builder, and that is where the weekend evaporates.
coreLoopDIY: You describe a business, an LLM returns a sitemap plus an ordered list of section types per page, and the tool assembles those from your local Tailwind component library into previewable, exportable pages.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
Node 20 and a willingness to live in Tailwind
You writing or borrowing the initial component library; the generator is only as good as its sections
Comfort editing JSX by hand for the last 20 percent
whatYouLose: The curated library itself: hundreds of sections that were designed, tested across breakpoints, and actually look coherent next to each other
Webflow clipboard paste, which is a proprietary format and the entire reason many people subscribe
Style presets that recolor and re-type an entire site consistently in one click
Someone else maintaining the components as Tailwind and framework versions drift
moatNotes: The defensible asset is a design library, not an algorithm. Generation is commodity; the sections are labor.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the output is production-ready and matches whatever tool the rest of the team lives in. Agencies buying Relume are buying speed on client work, and a local generator with twenty homemade sections does not survive a client presentation the way a library of hundreds of polished ones does. The Webflow paste flow in particular is a genuine lock: nobody is reverse engineering that on a Saturday and keeping it working. If you code your own frontends and only need structure plus a starting point, the subscription is harder to justify.
notes: The generator is a weekend, the library is a career.
prompt:
Build a local-only AI site scaffolder called sectionsmith. Stack: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, no database, no auth, no telemetry.

Core loop:
1. A single page at / with a textarea where I describe a business or project, plus selects for tone (clean, bold, editorial) and page count.
2. On submit, call an LLM through a server action to return strict JSON: a sitemap (array of pages with name, slug, purpose) and for each page an ordered array of section slots, where each slot names a component from a fixed allowlist and includes the copy for it (headline, subhead, bullets, cta labels, testimonial text, faq pairs).
3. Validate that JSON with zod. If a returned component name is not in the allowlist, drop the slot and log it. Never let the model invent component names into the render path.
4. Render the assembled pages in an iframe preview with a viewport toggle: mobile 390, tablet 768, desktop 1440.
5. An Export button writes real files to ./out: one .tsx per page importing from components/sections, plus a shared tokens file.

Component library: hand-write 16 sections in components/sections, each a typed React component taking props, each responsive and using CSS variables for color and radius. Cover: navbar, hero centered, hero split, logo cloud, feature grid, feature alternating, stats band, testimonial single, testimonial grid, pricing three tier, faq accordion, cta band, contact with form markup only, team grid, blog card list, footer. Keep them plain and confident, no animation libraries, no icon packs, inline SVG only.

Tokens: a themes.ts exporting three token sets (clean, bold, editorial) that set font stack, base color, accent, radius, and section spacing. Switching tone swaps tokens only, never component code.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: Webflow clipboard export, Figma export, drag and drop editing, image generation, deploying anything, user accounts, analytics.

Secrets: read ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from .env.local, ship .env.example, never hardcode keys. Write a README with setup in five lines and an honest note that the output quality is capped by the 16 sections and that adding sections is the real work.
